rv.q: Stiles not only gets the best number of the night — a knock-out song about menopause that will delight both the peri and the post — she gets off the best snark gags in the script.

Iceboy! or The Completely Untrue Story of How Eugene O’Neill Came to Write “The Iceman Cometh” is an outrageously inventive, joy-charged burst of musical comedy that proves Goodman Theatre can still surprise us in the best possible ways.
With JoAnn M. Hunter’s choreography, a terrific ensemble drives “Iceboy” to a big and satisfying finish and a promising future.
Just in time for summer and a blistering heatwave, ICEBOY is a refreshing escape from the ordinary and predictable.
It's one of the funniest, well-produced comedies of the year.
It’s a frothy nightcap to a year of successful productions, and a nice way to kick off the Goodman’s next act.
This new musical comedy, now enjoying its world premiere as the finale production of the Goodman Theatre’s Centennial season, is a whole lot of fun.

Unfortunately, “Iceboy!” by composer/lyricist Mark Hollmann (“Urinetown”), lyricist/book writer Jay Reiss (“The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee”) and writer Erin Quinn Purcell is not yet the ideal conduit for the considerable gifts these real-life spouses possess.
Despite the whimsy, the production still feels like a work-in-progress, trying to wrangle various comedic threads into a cohesive narrative.
Iceboy! is a cheeky romp that is charming, unpredictable, and full of life.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this gleefully absurd musical as a hysterical, joyfully strange theatrical confection that delivers razor-sharp comedy and laugh-out-loud moments, with powerhouse stars Megan Mullally and Nick Offerman lighting up the stage.
